issues.description: The template's TODO comment for the position calculation (main) instructs the student to place the resulting address in EAX, but the problem statement explicitly requires the computed address to be in ESI (and to use mov ecx, [esi]). The template's later code and the solution both expect the address in ESI (they push esi for later use and read [esi]). This conflicting instruction in the template will confuse students: if they follow the template comment and compute the address into EAX, the subsequent code (which expects ESI) will read the wrong memory location and the program behavior/printing will be incorrect.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the template's instruction consistent with the problem statement and the rest of the template code: change the TODO comment to require the computed pixel address to be placed in ESI (not EAX), and clarify register-preservation guidance accordingly. Concretely, replace the comment at template_repository/pixel.asm lines ~100-102 with instructions matching the problem: (EAX:x, EBX:y) compute address -> ESI, preserve registers you modify (except EAX/EBX as inputs), then use mov ecx, [esi] to read the pixel. Alternatively, if you prefer to return the address in EAX, update the rest of the template (push/pop and later uses) and the problem statement to expect EAX — but keep all artifacts consistent.

issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to place the computed pixel memory address into ESI and then read/write via [ESI] (it explicitly says "Ergebnis nach ESI" and shows mov ecx, [esi]). The template's in-place comment for the calculation (main TODO) instead tells students the result should be in EAX ("result (address) in EAX"). The solution implementation uses ESI to hold the computed pixel address. This register mismatch (ESI vs. EAX) for the single conceptual entity "computed pixel memory address" creates a direct mapping confusion: students following the template comment will compute the address into EAX while later code and the reference solution expect the address in ESI, leading to incorrect implementations and runtime errors.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the register choice consistent across all artifacts. Prefer aligning the template comment with the problem statement and solution by changing the template's TODO comment (and any guidance) to indicate that the computed pixel address should be placed in ESI (e.g., change "result (address) in EAX" to "result (address) in ESI"). Alternatively, if EAX is preferred, update the problem statement and the solution implementation to consistently use EAX. The simplest fix: update template_repository/pixel.asm line with the TODO to request the result in ESI so students and the solution match the problem text.
